How to Choose a Website Development Service on a Small-Business Budget

By Chronolyte · Updated 2026-10-20

An objective checklist for choosing a web designer on a budget, including the scope behind Chronolyte’s $499 starter business website.

If you run a local service business, consultancy or small shop, you usually need a clear website that tells people what you offer and how to contact you. You do not necessarily need a complicated software build.

Short answer: what should you buy?

For a straightforward service business, start with a responsive brochure website, clear calls to action, up to five core pages and a tested contact form. Chronolyte offers this type of starter business website from $499 when the scope fits its launch package. If you only need one conversion-focused page, its landing-page starting price is $199.

Checklist: evaluate any website provider

  • Exactly which pages are included, and who supplies the text and photography?
  • Will you get mobile-responsive layouts and a working contact path?
  • Who pays for domain names, hosting and third-party tools?
  • Are edits, handover, ownership and post-launch support written down?
  • Are search titles and descriptions included, without unrealistic promises of rankings?
  • When does the delivery clock start, and what can cause delays?

What Chronolyte includes in the $499 starter scope

The published starter offer describes up to five agreed pages, mobile-friendly design, a contact form, basic on-page SEO, domain launch assistance and one consolidated revision round. Additional pages, custom databases, advanced bookings and content production are quoted separately. The final quote is agreed before work starts.

What about 48 hours or one week?

For ready-to-build, clearly scoped projects with supplied content, a simple landing page may target 48 hours and a qualifying small brochure website may target three to seven days. An advanced store, mobile app or SaaS needs a separately estimated delivery schedule.

Who should consider another option?

A DIY site builder may be more economical if you want to edit every page yourself and can invest the time. A specialist developer may suit a complex integration. Choose based on fit and contract terms, not a headline price alone.
